newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of March 10, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

MAC WEEK - Apple Computer Inc CEO Gil Amelio sent a confidential memo to employees that he will answer all their urgent questions about the company's reorganization Friday, and he pledged to announce the total cost in jobs and dollars of its dramatic restructuring, Mac Week reported March 10.

Apple is working on a sequel to its current operating system, Version 7.6, with a new version called 7.61 that will run on Macs with the Motorola 68030, 68040 and Power PC processors, Mac Week reported. The PowerMac 9600, 8600 and 4400 and PowerBook 3400C do not work with the Mac OS 7.6 but are expected to run on 7.61.

PC WEEK - Microsoft Corp will demonstrate for the first time a set of software technologies that would recude the inconvenience of managing personal computer settings, PC Week reported in the March 10 issue.

Microsoft executives had planned to release the so-called zero administration initiative with the next major release of the Windows NT operating system but decided to release it earlier as an answer to a new generation of computers based on Java software.

COMPUTERWORLD - Microsoft is turning up the heat on corporate users to replace older Windows 3.1 programs and move to the more advanced Windows NT and Windows 95 systems, Computerworld reported in its March 10 issue.

In recent months, Microsoft has quit developing versions of products like Microsoft Office and the Visual Basic computer language programming tools for Windows 3.1, even though 80 percent of large corporate users still depend on the older programs.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - International Business Machines Corp will package various services and financing for large resellers to make it easier for them to track invoices, Computer Reseller News reported in its March 10 issue. The plan, code-named Project Spruce, is an effort to stave off similar efforts from rivals Compaq Computer Corp and Dell Computer Corp.
Microsoft has pushed back the introduction of the next major revision of the Windows NT operating system to at least the first quarter of 1998, according to developers briefed by Microsoft.
INFOWORLD - Microsoft plans to announce an agreement with Hewlett-Packard Co March 19 to improve Windows NT management, particularly in higher-level networks, InfoWorld reported March 10.

Apple will eliminate its MessagePad and Performa models, among other products, InfoWorld reported. The publication also said Apple is considering restructuring to be more like a holding company with independent operating units.

INFORMATION WEEK - The discovery of security flaws in Microsoft's Internet Explorer browser and in Sun Microsystem Inc's Java Virtual Machine raises new questions about corporate vulnerability, Information Week reported March 10.
Compaq is scrapping plans to build network computers and putting its efforts behind low-cost PCs and the forthcoming NetPC, Information Week reported.

EE TIMES - Motorola Inc's Computer Group is readying motherboards that will be powered by Intel's Pentium processor, not the PowerPC processors developed by IBM, Motorola and Apple, EE Times reported March 10.

It's time for U.S. broadcasters to put up or shut up, as digital television moves from the demo phase to deployment, as a live demonstration of high definition TV will headline the National Association of Broadcasters conference next month, EE Times reported March 10.

INTERACTIVE WEEK - The traffic-choked Internet could get a much-needed high-speed lane as early as this summer with a new series of super-fast routing centers, or points of presence, Interactive Week reported March 10.

America Online may charge subscribers additionally to use its gaming areas, and it is conducting focus groups to determine whether to charge extra for all or part of game-area usage, Interactive Week reported.
